questions.q: Why does this lesson say 'single org is just the best practice for most companies' is a weak answer to the ownership question?
options: Because it doesn't trace to a specific requirement, names no rejected alternative, and asserts a universal rule the course has already shown is not true
Because it is too long and detailed
Because single org actually is the wrong decision for LTV Global
Because board members never ask about org strategy
questions.explain: The weak answer fails every evaluation domain at once: no requirements traceability, no named rejected alternative, and it contradicts Lesson 7's own point that single-vs-multi-org is a genuine tradeoff, not a default best practice.

questions.q: In the EMEA/GDPR mock question, what makes the strong answer stronger than a simple 'No, because our security is good'?
options: It is much shorter
It avoids mentioning GDPR entirely
It names the specific combination of controls (OWD, role hierarchy, field-level security, Shield Platform Encryption, data-residency NFRs) rather than asserting a vague conclusion
It recommends giving EMEA its own org after all
questions.explain: The strong answer names the actual combination of mechanisms responsible for the outcome, which withstands follow-up questioning; a vague assurance invites exactly the kind of drilling that reveals unprepared reasoning.

questions.q: Why can a sales rep with full Account access still be unable to see a customer's credit score, per the mock answer?
options: Because credit scores are stored outside Salesforce entirely
Because field-level security is evaluated independently of record-level access, and credit-score fields are restricted to Equipment Financing profiles specifically
Because the sales rep's role sits below the customer in the hierarchy
Because Account access never includes any custom fields
questions.explain: The mock answer explains that record-level access and field-level security are two different gates answering two different questions — full Account visibility does not override field-level restrictions.

questions.q: What are the four self-scoring checks this lesson proposes for any defense answer?
options: Length, vocabulary, tone, and volume
Agreement with the board member, brevity, formality, and a closing summary
Speed, confidence, eye contact, and humor
A direct answer first, the actual reasoning, the rejected alternative where relevant, and concrete evidence
questions.explain: The lesson's four self-scoring checks are: direct answer first, stated reasoning (not just a conclusion), the rejected alternative where relevant, and concrete supporting evidence.

questions.q: What is the key difference between what object/record-level access answers versus what field-level security answers, per the mock answer in this lesson?
options: Object/record-level access answers 'can you see this record at all,' while field-level security answers 'of the fields on a record you can see, which ones you can actually see'
They answer the exact same question and are fully redundant
Field-level security only applies to external portal users, never internal reps
Object-level access always overrides field-level security when they conflict
questions.explain: The mock answer explicitly distinguishes these as two separate gates answering two separate questions, which is why having full Account access doesn't automatically grant visibility into a specific restricted field.
